title: 26 CFR § 1.704-3, Contributed property (2025 annual edition)
publisher: U.S. Department of the Treasury; 2025 CFR edition hosted by GovInfo
source_classification: Treasury regulation; primary federal tax authority
questions: multi-year tax and book capital effects
inspected_summary: The regulation defines built-in gain/loss from contribution-date book value and tax basis, requires reasonable methods to prevent shifting tax consequences, and supplies a multiyear traditional-method example. In Example 1, after $400 first-year tax depreciation allocated to B, the remaining $5,400 built-in gain is allocated to A on a $9,000 year-two sale; if the partnership then liquidates with $19,000 cash distributed equally, A’s $9,400 outside basis yields $100 gain and B’s $9,600 basis yields $100 loss. Curative and remedial methods address ceiling-rule distortion differently, with consistency and reasonableness conditions.

title: Handbook: Revenue recognition
source_classification: Professional interpretive handbook; summarizes FASB/SEC staff meeting views and KPMG conclusions
questions: ASC 606 variable consideration versus equity ownership model
inspected_summary: Question 2.3.80 says “It depends.” KPMG recounts the FASB members’ 2016 TRG view that asset-management performance fees in carried-interest form were intended within Topic 606 and the SEC Observer’s statement that an ownership model could be acceptable on specific facts if Topics 810, 323 or other relevant guidance are fully applied. KPMG’s 2025 interpretive conclusion is that private and public entities may consistently elect between Topic 606 and an ownership model; if Topic 606 has been applied, voluntary change to ownership is generally difficult to support. This is KPMG’s interpretation of 2016 staff comments, not FASB/SEC authoritative guidance.
